items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision slots and c1 together say what to do (ship Brisk-S few-shot), why (the only one of nine inside all three gates; options_dominance confirms it is the sole survivor and dominant), what it costs ($1,200 a month) and the main risk (overall accuracy clears by 0.7 points with no stated interval). why_not names why each rival is out, and every figure checks against the snapshot.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (sole survivor) -> c2 (the cheap rival fails only on complex news) -> c3 (every more accurate option breaks latency) -> c4 (the pick's own weak lines) -> c5 (lever that points the next step) follows logically. The explore outcomes match decision_sensitivity exactly: cell floor flips to Nano-XS few-shot at <=76.7% and to no call above 82.9%; overall goes to no call above 90.7%; raising p95 never moves the call. Two seams are listed under items 4 and 7: the omitted list says model-lever effects are left out while c5's block shows them, and c5's lead sentence is contradicted by its own Brisk-S rows.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The pick's weak axes are up front: the 0.7-point overall clearance appears in the lede, flag, caveats, watch and c4, and the complex news cell (82.9%, weakest for all nine configurations, which I verified) appears in the recommendation and c4. c2's per-cell differences are captioned as unpaired and uncorrected, 'a lead, not a confirmed finding'. If anything the overall-accuracy risk is overstated (see item 5). Two places overreach: c5's 'the lever' (item 7) and the c2 heatmap caption that calls the pair 'the two cheapest options inside the latency budget' (item 7).

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: I checked each omission against the snapshot. Traffic-weighted accuracy ranks all nine the same way (pick 92.2% vs Nano-XS few-shot 92.0%; the order is unchanged and it is not a gate). Macro F1 ranks the same way (89.6 vs 89.0, same order). count.examples = 0. Atlas-M costs $180-$610 per 1M and fails p95 by 170-1052 ms. None of these would change the call. Two weak spots: the confusion-table reason ('err almost identically on each axis') states a fact no tool reads from this snapshot, so it can't be checked, and 'Model-lever effects and their interactions' is listed as omitted although c5's block prints all of them.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: All four snapshot caveats (no_control, point_estimate:overall, point_estimate:p95, best_of_n) are carried with material_if clauses, and the overall-accuracy and best-of-n ones flow into watch and next[0]. Unpaired, uncorrected comparison intervals are stated in Method and the c2 caption. One gap: balanced accuracy is exactly the unweighted mean of the nine cell accuracies (816.0/9 = 90.67, and 90.1 for Nano-XS few-shot). Those cells carry stated half-widths, so a 95% half-width of about 0.31 points is derivable today (sqrt(sum hw^2)/9). That puts the interval at about 90.4-91.0, wholly above 90%. The report treats sampling noise on overall accuracy as unresolved when the data in hand nearly settle it. Selection (best of nine) is the real residual risk.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each of the three steps names an experiment or a declaration and says what it settles. next[0]: a fresh held-out run with an interval settles the overall gate and best-of-n. next[1]: complex news examples for Nano-XS few-shot settle whether the cheap option clears the floor. next[2]: the owner declares whether $1,143/month is worth a second iteration. Weak spots: next[1] says 're-run that cell', but what it settles needs overall accuracy to 'hold', so the whole arm must be re-run (and a prompt tuned to one cell is itself a new best-of-n selection). next[0]'s noise half is partly answerable now (item 5).

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c1's gate_matrix, c2's heatmap and compare bars, and c3's gate_scatter are the right blocks, and the counterfactual holds for each. Three blocks fall short. (a) The c2 heatmap caption is false: inside the latency budget Nano-XS zero-shot ($1.3/1M), Nano-XS few-shot ($1.9), Nano-XS rubric ($4.6) and Brisk-S zero-shot ($28) are all cheaper than the pick ($40), so the pick is the most expensive of the five, not one of the 'two cheapest'. (b) The c4 settle table prints '—' for overall accuracy's distance, so the line c4 calls 'narrowest' shows no distance in the block meant to prove it. The claim would read the same if that distance were 10 points, and 8 of the table's 16 columns are all '—'. (c) c5's levers block prints model effects and interactions the omitted list says are left out. Its interaction rows are mislabelled (rows 13 and 14 share one label with values +7.2 and +0.2). It also contradicts c5's lead claim: for Brisk-S the rubric lifts overall accuracy more than few-shot (+5.5 vs +4.7).

findings.finding: The heatmap caption calls Brisk-S few-shot and Nano-XS few-shot 'the two cheapest options inside the latency budget'. That is false. Inside the budget the pick ($40 per 1M) is the costliest of five; Nano-XS zero-shot ($1.3), Nano-XS rubric ($4.6) and Brisk-S zero-shot ($28) are cheaper. The true description is 'the only two inside both the latency budget and the overall accuracy gate'. As written, the caption flatters the pick's cost position.

'Few-shot examples are the lever that lifts the small models' is contradicted by the block's own rows: for Brisk-S, zero->rubric is +5.5 and zero->few-shot +4.7. The rubric is out for Brisk-S on latency, not accuracy. 'The rubric ... takes much of it back ... against few-shot alone' also implies the rubric is stacked on few-shot. The arm settings make it a separate prompt level (Nano-XS zero->rubric +5.7 vs zero->few +11.9): the rubric lifts less, it doesn't take a lift back. Restate the claim as 'on Nano-XS, few-shot lifts overall accuracy far more than the rubric (+11.9 vs +5.7); on Brisk-S the two are close'.

The levers block prints model effects and both interaction groups, which omitted[5] says are left out. Restrict the query to the prompt lever, or drop the omitted entry. The interaction rows are also mislabelled by the renderer: rows 13 and 14 both read 'prompt effect, across model, at Nano-XS · Zero-shot less at Brisk-S · Zero-shot' with values +7.2 and +0.2, and rows 10-12 name arms where they mean prompt levels.

The overall-accuracy interval is derivable from figures already on the page. Balanced accuracy is the unweighted mean of the nine cell accuracies (Brisk-S few-shot: 816.0/9 = 90.67; Nano-XS few-shot: 810.9/9 = 90.1), and the cells carry stated binomial half-widths that check against n. That gives a 95% half-width of about 0.31 points, so the interval is about 90.4-91.0, wholly above the 90% line. The lede, flag, caveat point_estimate:overall and next[0] all present sampling noise on this figure as open. Either state the derived interval (and narrow the material_if and next[0] to the best-of-nine selection and fresh-case drift), or say why the cells can't be combined.

The settle table is c4's evidence, but it prints '—' for overall accuracy's distance (+0.7 is known: criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap). So the block doesn't show the 'narrowest line' half of the claim. Its eight trials and repeats columns are all '—' and add width without content. The block note also says 'Each bar' on a table. Show the overall distance, even marked 'no interval', and drop the empty columns.

next[1] says 're-run that cell', but its 'settles' needs overall accuracy to hold, so the whole Nano-XS arm must be re-run on fresh cases. A prompt tuned to complex news is a new selection and inherits the best-of-n caveat. Say both.

omitted[2] asserts that 'Brisk-S few-shot and Nano-XS few-shot err almost identically on each axis', but no tool reads per-axis or confusion figures from this snapshot (measure_read refuses strata; only per-cell accuracy is held). Either cite figures that support it or reduce the reason to 'the snapshot holds no per-axis or joint confusion figures'.

Printing. The lede and watch read 'clears overall accuracy by only +0.7 points' and '+0.7 points over'; use |abs so prose doesn't carry a sign. why_not reads 'the pick costs 21.05 times as much', which is false precision; '21 times' or 'about twenty times' would do. The gate_scatter labels the overall-accuracy line 'floor 90%', while the page uses 'floor' only for the per-cell floor.

invariant_concerns: Invariant 1: all 29 figure keys read through figure_keys_check, none refused or unstated. omitted[2] makes a factual assertion (near-identical per-axis errors) that no figure key in the snapshot can back. It contains no number, so this is not a breach, but it can't be checked.

Invariant 2: every block renders, but c5's levers block has duplicated or ambiguous interaction labels (rows 13 and 14 identical with different values), and c4's table note refers to 'bars'. These are renderer text defects to raise with the kit, not the analyst.
Invariant 6: report.json carries Method but no explicit full-results appendix entry; I assume the page generates it and can't verify that from the doc alone.
